To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we proposed a 128-b bit-slice RSFQ AES encryption accelerator based on the lookup table method.
the proposed accelerator is the smallest AES accelerator based on RSFQ circuits.
the proposed AES encryption accelerator based on RSFQ circuits is suitable for high-speed and high-security applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a 128-b RSFQ AES encryption accelerator.
the design and implementation of a high-speed and low-power RSFQ accelerator for AES encryption.
the logic design and simulation of the 128-b AES encryption accelerator based on the RSFQ circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is a good example of a novel design of an RSFQ AES accelerator that is based on bit-sliced architecture.
the proposed method is very effective in reducing the hardware cost of AES encryption accelerator.
the proposed accelerator has a low power consumption, high operating speed, and low hardware cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a 128-b rapid-single flux quantum AES encryption accelerator based on the bit-slice architecture.
a 128-b RSFQ AES encryption accelerator based on the proposed lookup table method has been designed and simulated at logic level.
the proposed AES accelerator can be used as an important part of a secure communication system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bit-slice architecture can be applied to RSFQ logic design and can be used to accelerate AES encryption.
the AES accelerator based on the bit-slice architecture can be implemented by using only 136 558 Josephson junctions, which is the smallest number of JJs reported to date.
we can reduce nearly 40% of the hardware resource compared with the traditional method.
